# Book Recommendations (book recommendations MCP server)

> "What should I read next?" answered for AI agents: topic recommendations from millions of works (OpenLibrary), blind-date serendipity spins hooked by first sentences, and free public-domain classics (Gutenberg). Zero API keys.

## Installation
- UVX: `uvx book-recommendations`
- NPX: `npx -y book-recommendations`
- Curl installer: `curl -fsSL https://book-recommendations.builditwithai.xyz/install | bash`
- Repository: https://github.com/surendranb/book-recommendations

## When to use
- "what should I read next" / "recommend books about X" / "books like Y" -> recommend(topic)
- "surprise me with a book" -> blind_date()
- "something classic I can read right now for free" -> free_classics(topic?)

## Primary Tools
- `recommend(topic, count, exclude)`: book recommendations with rating, subjects, first sentence, and read_now flags (free/borrowable at archive.org).
- `blind_date(count, seed, exclude)`: random shelf at random depth; present first_sentence first, then the reveal.
- `free_classics(topic, count)`: public-domain books with read-now URLs (fail-soft: points to archive.org alternatives when gutendex is down).
- `skills_list()` / `skill_read(name)`: presentation + error-recovery playbooks.

## Notes for agents
- Relay why_picked verbatim; it says how the book was chosen.
- Blind-date picks get the two-beat reveal: hook (first sentence, subjects, era), then title/author.

## Environment Variables
- `BOOK_RECOMMENDATIONS_TELEMETRY=false` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`: disable anonymous telemetry.
